title: Senior Go Backend Developer (f/m/d)
description: adjoe builds the technologies behind mobile apps growth and monetization. With our core product Playtime Arcade , we've become the global leader in rewarded advertising, an ad unit built on a simple premise: users earn real in-app rewards for engaging with new apps. The result is one of the most effective value exchanges in adtech, connecting advertisers and publishers with over 770 million users annually. Engineering the sub-millisecond decision engine that powers 200 million daily ad interactions The Demand Core team builds the infrastructure that determines which of our thousands of active advertising campaigns are relevant to a user the moment they open our ad unit Playtime. At our scale, system latency is a business failure, downtime means advertisers stop spending, users stop earning rewards, and publisher revenue stalls. You will build and operate the services that power these decisions 200 million times every day . Go microservices load the active ad campaign catalog into memory, evaluating 40+ targeting constraints and 30+ real-time signals , geo, fraud status, budget caps to rank potential user performance in milliseconds . Beyond campaign distribution, the team owns the entire ad interaction chain: processing clicks, views, MMP postbacks from Adjust and AppsFlyer , and in-app events that trigger rewards. These events are broadcasted through a hybrid messaging architecture using SNS/SQS and Kafka , directly powering our advertiser dashboards, publisher reward payouts, and ad campaign scoring pipelines, all backed by DynamoDB . Your Mission & Who We Are Looking For: Production Golang Systems Expertise: You bring 5+ years of backend development experience, including at least 3 years writing Go in production distributed environments. You will build and maintain our +99% Go microservice architecture—interfacing with our TypeScript/React frontend—to reliably handle 2+ million daily publisher interactions and scale beyond hundreds of millions of monthly active users. High-Throughput Event Streaming: You have hands-on experience designing asynchronous microservice communication using event buses like Kafka, SQS/SNS, and Kinesis. You will build pipelines to collect billions of daily API events and aggregate them into our data lake for sub-second querying. High-Scale Data & API Optimization: You understand database internals and low-level web standards (HTTP protocol, Encoding, Regular Expressions). You will optimize queries across hundreds of terabytes of data across DynamoDB, MySQL, Druid, and Athena to reduce API response times and expose transparent, well-documented open APIs to enterprise partners. Data Science & Algorithmic Integration: You quickly grasp complex technical topics and applied mathematics. You will partner directly with our Data Science team to translate and integrate machine learning algorithms into adjoe’s core application, optimizing real-time ad targeting. Collaborative Technical Communication: You communicate fluently and precisely in spoken and written English. You will actively participate in peer code reviews and technical knowledge sharing across an international backend engineering team. Plus: Infrastructure & Cloud Tooling: Hands-on experience with Terraform (Infrastructure as Code), Docker containerization, or serverless infrastructure. 🌎 We welcome applications from talent worldwide and provide relocation support to Hamburg, Germany for those ready to join our team. What’s in It for You? At adjoe, you’re not here to just close JIRA tickets, you’re helping build the infrastructure behind one of the most impactful platforms in adtech. The systems you work on will reach hundreds of millions of users and power billions of decisions every day. Go Big. Own projects with impact on 770M users and push adtech boundaries. Move Fast. Ship solutions multiple times a day, learn from results, and keep momentum. Be Direct. Solve problems openly and collaborate across teams. Thrive Together. Grow with a diverse, global team of people from over 40 different countries that learn from each other. Have Fun. Celebrate wins, enjoy daily victories, and bring your energy. description: Regional Sales Manager, DACH (m/w/d) Regional Role · Remote, based in the DACH region · Reports to: Sales Director About Everfield Everfield acquires and builds vertical SaaS businesses across Europe. Our portfolio spans more than 40 companies serving niche markets where software is mission-critical. We take a long-term ownership approach: we buy, invest, and build. We don't flip. Seven companies are in DACH, and we expect continuous growth in portfolio size and performance across all regions. We are building a small, high-impact HQ revenue team responsible for lifting the commercial capability of our portfolio companies: setting standards, identifying risk, and accelerating performance. The role reports to Everfield's Sales Director, who owns consistency of the revenue system across all regions, and works day to day with the region's General Director and the CEOs of its Business Units. The Opportunity The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) is a cluster-level revenue operator responsible for improving sales execution and accelerating organic revenue growth across a group of portfolio companies. The role partners directly with CEOs and Business Unit leaders to strengthen pipeline discipline, improve forecast accuracy, and raise commercial maturity across the region. This is not purely an advisory role. Alongside the regional remit, the RSM is expected to take direct sales management responsibility inside Business Units where that is the fastest route to growth, giving smaller commercial teams access to experienced sales leadership they would not otherwise have. As the region scales, the ambition is that one person can hold the sales management role on behalf of several Business Units at once, applying a standard across all of them. Success is reflected in improved revenue predictability, stronger pipeline discipline, and sustained bookings growth across Business Units. How the Role Operates • Two levels, one standard. The regional remit is constant: diagnostics, pipeline discipline, forecast integrity, and commercial governance across every Business Unit in the cluster. Beyond it, the role flexes. In some Business Units you will coach and support an existing sales manager. In others you will hold the sales management role yourself. • Direct team leadership where it is needed. Where you act as sales manager, you own the team, the pipeline, the forecast, and the number, in the same way a local sales manager would, and you report into that Business Unit's CEO for delivery while remaining accountable to Everfield for how the work is done. • You are not a seller. You do not carry a personal quota and you are not measured on deals you close yourself. You are measured on what the teams you lead and support deliver. • Reporting. You report to Everfield's Sales Director for standards, priorities, and development. The role is a shared resource for the region rather than a function serving any single Business Unit, acting in close partnership with Group Directors, CEOs, and sales teams. What You Will Do Sales Execution & Commercial Acceleration • Drive new and expansion bookings growth across the cluster, with consistent attention to prospecting, opportunity development, and account growth. • Act as sales manager for one or more Business Units: run the weekly rhythm, set priorities, coach the team, and hold sellers to their number. • Reduce volatility in bookings performance and increase revenue consistency across the cluster. • Strengthen proactive sales behaviour across outbound, account expansion, renewals and opportunity reactivation. • Improve sales execution across the full funnel, from lead generation through to closing and account retention. • Embed sales methodology and qualification standards, and hold teams to them through evidence rather than instruction. • Lead deal/pipeline reviews and targeted coaching to improve win rates, shorten cycle times, and build seller capability. Pipeline Discipline & Forecast Integrity • Improve forecast reliability across Business Units, working toward 5% variance or better. • Define and apply opportunity qualification standards and run structured pipeline reviews. • Ensure pipeline visibility reflects realistic execution capacity, and raise revenue risks early to Business Units and Everfield leadership, always paired with a recommended course of action rather than an open flag. • Monitor sustained underperformance patterns and ensure corrective action plans are implemented in time to matter. Revenue Standards & Definitions • Act as guardian of Everfield's revenue definitions in the region: what counts as a booking, how new name is separated from back to base, how recurring value is recognised, and what enters the pipeline in the first place. • Hold those definitions consistently, including where a Business Unit's own commercial logic pushes against them, and fix the incentive, target, or CRM design underneath rather than bending the measurement. • Make the cluster comparable to every other region, so performance can be read the same way across the portfolio. Commercial Governance • Ensure transparency in quota design, attainment measurement, and sales capacity planning. • Support commission structure alignment with business goals. • Contribute to annual, quarterly, and monthly commercial planning by reality-checking growth assumptions against pipeline health, execution capacity, and historical feasibility. Commercial Diagnostics • Diagnose revenue performance across segments, teams, and funnel stages, identifying where revenue is generated, stalled, or lost. • Produce a written diagnostic and prioritised action plan for each Business Unit you take on, naming the problem, the cause, the cost of inaction, the action, the owner, and the date. • Prioritise your own time across the cluster on distance to target, materiality to the region, and whether a documented plan already exists. • Provide feedback on pricing discipline, discounting practices, packaging effectiveness, and ICP conversion efficiency. • Translate performance signals into executive-level recommendations and commercial action plans. CEO & General Director Partnership • Act as strategic commercial partner to CEOs and Business Unit leaders, representing Everfield's revenue expectations and performance discipline. • Challenge growth assumptions constructively and escalate persistent underperformance when required. What Success Looks Like In the first 12 months: • Full visibility into the commercial funnel, aligned with HQ reporting standards. • Acceleration of organic recurring revenue growth across the region. • Improved reliability of pipeline data and forecast accuracy. • Sales pipelines that more accurately predict bookings performance. • At least one Business Unit where you hold sales management directly and the team delivers against its number. • Reliable visibility of quota attainment and seller productivity. • Deal reviews embedded across portfolio sales teams, resulting in higher win rates and shorter sales cycles. • Revenue per seller increasing steadily across the cluster. • A documented, reusable set of playbooks and diagnostics that other regions can apply without starting again. What We Are Looking For • 6-10 years total experience in B2B SaaS revenue roles, with at least 3-4 years in a sales management position, accountable for a team's bookings performance and not only for personal pipeline contribution. • Track record of consistent revenue target attainment in a management role. You have owned a number and delivered against it, not only improved process quality. • Direct experience leading and developing a sales team, including hiring, coaching, and managing underperformance. You will do this again here, inside our Business Units. • Track record of implementing structured pipeline management: defining stage criteria, enforcing qualification standards, running deal reviews, and improving forecast reliability. • Experience diagnosing revenue performance across the full funnel: understanding where deals are lost, why cycles extend, and what structural issues limit growth. • Manages through CRM data: uses pipeline data to run structured deal reviews, identify risk, and hold sellers accountable to data quality. Familiar with Salesforce or HubSpot as a management tool. • Experience working with senior stakeholders (CEOs, founders, or general managers) on commercial performance, including navigating organisational resistance and earning trust before driving change. • Experience adapting sales management approach across companies at different sales maturity levels: able to calibrate coaching, process rigour, and expectations to fit the context. • German fluency required, with professional English for work across the group. Regional Role · Remote, based in the DACH region · Reports to: Sales Director

About Everfield

Everfield acquires and builds vertical SaaS businesses across Europe. Our portfolio spans more than 40 companies serving niche markets where software is mission-critical. We take a long-term ownership approach: we buy, invest, and build. We don't flip. Seven companies are in DACH, and we expect continuous growth in portfolio size and performance across all regions.

We are building a small, high-impact HQ revenue team responsible for lifting the commercial capability of our portfolio companies: setting standards, identifying risk, and accelerating performance. The role reports to Everfield's Sales Director, who owns consistency of the revenue system across all regions, and works day to day with the region's General Director and the CEOs of its Business Units.

The Opportunity

The Regional Sales Manager (RSM) is a cluster-level revenue operator responsible for improving sales execution and accelerating organic revenue growth across a group of portfolio companies. The role partners directly with CEOs and Business Unit leaders to strengthen pipeline discipline, improve forecast accuracy, and raise commercial maturity across the region.

This is not purely an advisory role. Alongside the regional remit, the RSM is expected to take direct sales management responsibility inside Business Units where that is the fastest route to growth, giving smaller commercial teams access to experienced sales leadership they would not otherwise have. As the region scales, the ambition is that one person can hold the sales management role on behalf of several Business Units at once, applying a standard across all of them.

Success is reflected in improved revenue predictability, stronger pipeline discipline, and sustained bookings growth across Business Units.

How the Role Operates

• Two levels, one standard. The regional remit is constant: diagnostics, pipeline discipline, forecast integrity, and commercial governance across every Business Unit in the cluster. Beyond it, the role flexes. In some Business Units you will coach and support an existing sales manager. In others you will hold the sales management role yourself.

• Direct team leadership where it is needed. Where you act as sales manager, you own the team, the pipeline, the forecast, and the number, in the same way a local sales manager would, and you report into that Business Unit's CEO for delivery while remaining accountable to Everfield for how the work is done.

• You are not a seller. You do not carry a personal quota and you are not measured on deals you close yourself. You are measured on what the teams you lead and support deliver.

• Reporting. You report to Everfield's Sales Director for standards, priorities, and development. The role is a shared resource for the region rather than a function serving any single Business Unit, acting in close partnership with Group Directors, CEOs, and sales teams.

What You Will Do

Sales Execution & Commercial Acceleration

• Drive new and expansion bookings growth across the cluster, with consistent attention to prospecting, opportunity development, and account growth.

• Act as sales manager for one or more Business Units: run the weekly rhythm, set priorities, coach the team, and hold sellers to their number.

• Reduce volatility in bookings performance and increase revenue consistency across the cluster.

• Strengthen proactive sales behaviour across outbound, account expansion, renewals and opportunity reactivation.

• Improve sales execution across the full funnel, from lead generation through to closing and account retention.

• Embed sales methodology and qualification standards, and hold teams to them through evidence rather than instruction.

• Lead deal/pipeline reviews and targeted coaching to improve win rates, shorten cycle times, and build seller capability.

Pipeline Discipline & Forecast Integrity

• Improve forecast reliability across Business Units, working toward 5% variance or better.

• Define and apply opportunity qualification standards and run structured pipeline reviews.

• Ensure pipeline visibility reflects realistic execution capacity, and raise revenue risks early to Business Units and Everfield leadership, always paired with a recommended course of action rather than an open flag.

• Monitor sustained underperformance patterns and ensure corrective action plans are implemented in time to matter.

Revenue Standards & Definitions

• Act as guardian of Everfield's revenue definitions in the region: what counts as a booking, how new name is separated from back to base, how recurring value is recognised, and what enters the pipeline in the first place.

• Hold those definitions consistently, including where a Business Unit's own commercial logic pushes against them, and fix the incentive, target, or CRM design underneath rather than bending the measurement.

• Make the cluster comparable to every other region, so performance can be read the same way across the portfolio.

Commercial Governance

• Ensure transparency in quota design, attainment measurement, and sales capacity planning.

• Support commission structure alignment with business goals.

• Contribute to annual, quarterly, and monthly commercial planning by reality-checking growth assumptions against pipeline health, execution capacity, and historical feasibility.

Commercial Diagnostics

• Diagnose revenue performance across segments, teams, and funnel stages, identifying where revenue is generated, stalled, or lost.

• Produce a written diagnostic and prioritised action plan for each Business Unit you take on, naming the problem, the cause, the cost of inaction, the action, the owner, and the date.

• Prioritise your own time across the cluster on distance to target, materiality to the region, and whether a documented plan already exists.

• Provide feedback on pricing discipline, discounting practices, packaging effectiveness, and ICP conversion efficiency.

• Translate performance signals into executive-level recommendations and commercial action plans.

CEO & General Director Partnership

• Act as strategic commercial partner to CEOs and Business Unit leaders, representing Everfield's revenue expectations and performance discipline.

• Challenge growth assumptions constructively and escalate persistent underperformance when required.

What Success Looks Like

In the first 12 months:

• Full visibility into the commercial funnel, aligned with HQ reporting standards.

• Acceleration of organic recurring revenue growth across the region.

• Improved reliability of pipeline data and forecast accuracy.

• Sales pipelines that more accurately predict bookings performance.

• At least one Business Unit where you hold sales management directly and the team delivers against its number.

• Reliable visibility of quota attainment and seller productivity.

• Deal reviews embedded across portfolio sales teams, resulting in higher win rates and shorter sales cycles.

• Revenue per seller increasing steadily across the cluster.

• A documented, reusable set of playbooks and diagnostics that other regions can apply without starting again.

What We Are Looking For

• 6-10 years total experience in B2B SaaS revenue roles, with at least 3-4 years in a sales management position, accountable for a team's bookings performance and not only for personal pipeline contribution.

• Track record of consistent revenue target attainment in a management role. You have owned a number and delivered against it, not only improved process quality.

• Direct experience leading and developing a sales team, including hiring, coaching, and managing underperformance. You will do this again here, inside our Business Units.

• Track record of implementing structured pipeline management: defining stage criteria, enforcing qualification standards, running deal reviews, and improving forecast reliability.

• Experience diagnosing revenue performance across the full funnel: understanding where deals are lost, why cycles extend, and what structural issues limit growth.

• Manages through CRM data: uses pipeline data to run structured deal reviews, identify risk, and hold sellers accountable to data quality. Familiar with Salesforce or HubSpot as a management tool.

• Experience working with senior stakeholders (CEOs, founders, or general managers) on commercial performance, including navigating organisational resistance and earning trust before driving change.

• Experience adapting sales management approach across companies at different sales maturity levels: able to calibrate coaching, process rigour, and expectations to fit the context.

• German fluency required, with professional English for work across the group. European B2B SaaS market experience required.

• Commercial finance literacy is a strong advantage: reading a P&L, understanding revenue recognition, and being able to argue the return on a commercial investment.

• Private-equity-backed or multi-entity SaaS environment experience is a strong advantage.

Skills

• Structured coaching and seller development: designing and running structured 1:1s, deal reviews, and field accompaniment to build individual seller capability, not just inspect opportunities.

• Pipeline discipline and forecasting: reading a pipeline critically, identifying risk early, and improving forecast reliability.

• Change management: driving commercial process adoption across multiple teams, and building momentum without relying on formal authority.

• Documentation and knowledge scale: writing down what you diagnose and what you implement, in a form another person can pick up and run. Work that lives only in conversation does not scale across a portfolio, and anything you build for one Business Unit should be reusable in the next.

• Commercial planning and challenge: building a bottom-up view of what revenue targets are achievable, pressure-testing top-down assumptions, and presenting credible alternatives to leadership.

• Commercial storytelling: presenting clear, honest risk assessments to CEOs and senior leadership, and leading a review that drives decisions rather than just restating numbers.

  • Full Business proficiency in German and English is a must

Who You Are

• You lead teams and you influence without authority. You will manage sellers directly in some Business Units and hold no formal authority in others. Both need to work. You build trust quickly and drive change through credibility, clarity, and structured analysis.

• You are hands-on with sales execution. You are comfortable stepping into real deals, reviewing opportunities with sellers, and diagnosing pipeline issues directly with the team, without needing to be the person closing.

• You combine analytical thinking with practical commercial judgement. You interpret pipeline data, and you also understand the realities of getting deals done.

• You communicate clearly and directly. You raise commercial risks early, with a recommendation attached, and challenge assumptions constructively, including when performance doesn't meet expectations.

You are pragmatic in complex environments. Portfolio companies vary in maturity and commercial model. You bring discipline without imposing rigid process that doesn't fit the situation

description: Mapbox is the leading real-time location platform for a new generation of location-aware businesses. Mapbox is the only platform that equips organizations with the full set of tools to power the navigation of people, packages, and vehicles everywhere. Organizations use Mapbox applications, data, SDKs and APIs to create customized and immersive experiences that delight their customers. The team is developing 3D Live Navigation , an advanced navigation system that enhances traditional maps by integrating high-resolution 3D lane models, real-time sensor data, environmental models, and dynamic lighting conditions. We are leveraging feedback from millions of vehicles and aerial imagery to create a detailed and immersive 3D navigation experience. Additionally, we are working on integration with in-vehicle sensors and ADAS to provide precise lane-level guidance, hazard warnings, and improved situational awareness, helping drivers navigate complex roads more safely and efficiently. Learn more: mapbox.com/blog/mapbox-3d-navigation What You'll Do Develop real-time visualization of ADAS sensor data and HD lane-level navigation for Mapbox Navigation SDK, including implementation of simulation tools for testing various driving scenarios and sensor data playback. Assess minimum requirements for our automotive solutions and align them with reference platforms. Write clean, fast C++ code to integrate various data inputs required for our automotive navigation system product offerings, or provide custom-tailored solutions as needed. Implement and collaborate on new rendering and navigation features. Own full-stack development from data to navigation experience across various platforms and stacks. Fine-tune the automotive navigation experience through profiling and debugging techniques to extract the best performance from customer platforms. Work with technical counterparts at customers and partners to discover requirements, provide implementation recommendations, and debug integrations. Collaborate with internal teams to ensure best practices for cross-platform API design and performance tuning for specific hardware and software combinations. Improve the product’s performance, stability, maintainability, and simplicity. What We Believe are Important Traits for This Role Broad experience in software development, customer engagements, and automotive compliance standards. Strong technical expertise (6+ years) in modern and embedded C++. Proficient in rendering with a strong foundation in algorithms and performance optimization. Experienced with build systems like CMake and Gradle, and developing frameworks/developer tools. Excellent communication skills, capable of working effectively with distributed teams, customers, and partners (Fluent in English). description: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. Location This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with regular visits to customers across the DACH region. Team collaboration matters a lot to us. You will regularly spend time with the team in person, in Zurich and at our hubs, for team days, all-hands and offsites. These visits are financially supported by blp. Your Mission On our largest global rollouts, connectivity is what makes or breaks the program. These customers run several ERP systems across many entities and countries, with interfaces, master data and process variants that have grown over decades. Whether blp is usable on day one, and whether the first go-live holds its date, depends more on getting that landscape right than on almost anything else. You are the person who makes sure it is right. You sit opposite the customer's enterprise architects and IT leads, understand what their landscape actually does rather than what the documentation says, and shape the technical solution with them. Getting this right is relentless project management as much as architecture. Requirements on a landscape this size never arrive clear. You chase them until they are: pushing the customer's IT organization for answers, going back when an answer is vague, and refusing to let an assumption stand in for a decision. You spot the major developments and the roadblocks early, while there is still time to do something about them, and you put them in front of the Senior Project Manager and into the steering committee rather than discovering them in test. When you raise something, you bring the way through it. You prepare the discussion with the customer, make the implications clear in their language, and come with options. "We cannot do that and we will miss the go-live" is not the job. Working out what would make it possible, and what it costs, is. Where something exceeds the standard you prepare the decision rather than take it alone: options, effort, consequences, and a clear recommendation for the steering committee or for our engineering leadership. You are the strong technical counterpart for the customer's IT organization and for the Senior Project Manager. Both rely on you to know what is actually true. You work primarily up to the first go-live, where the solution design is either right or expensive, and you are staffed by process and landscape complexity rather than by deal size. A word on what you build. Our integration layer works like an iPaaS: connections are assembled as configuration on our own platform, specific to that customer, rather than written as code. You work in that layer yourself, so this is a hands-on role, and you document what you have configured so that the next person can understand and maintain it. What you do not do is write code that ships with the product. That distinction is what keeps a customer-specific solution from quietly becoming everyone's problem. Two roles sit either side of you and the handoffs are clean. With the Integrations Engineer: you define what the connection has to do and why, they build and operate it at that customer and own whether it runs. You hand them a specification, they come back with questions and constraints from the real system, and you resolve them together. When something breaks in their environment, it is theirs. When something is wrong in what was asked for, it is yours. With the Product Engineer: when a requirement cannot be met in configuration, or when the same requirement has now appeared at the third customer, you make the case for building it into the product. You write the specification, they build it, and you are the one who confirms it actually solves the customer problem it came from. After that it is part of the standard and you configure against it like anything else. Key Responsibilities Shape the technical solution with the customer, including their enterprise architects and IT leads. Turn business requirements into a clear, implementable specification. Drive requirements to clarity, relentlessly. Chase the customer's IT organization until an answer is specific enough to build on. Configure integrations on our platform where the standard covers it, and document what you have configured. Identify precisely where the standard does not cover a requirement, and judge whether it belongs in configuration or in the product. Identify major development needs and technical roadblocks early, and escalate them to the Senior Project Manager and into the steering committee while there is still time. Prepare those discussions with the customer: make the implications clear, and bring options rather than a refusal. Prepare scope decisions with options, effort and consequences, and bring a clear recommendation to the steering committee or to our engineering leadership. Specify what the Integrations Engineer builds at the customer, and resolve the constraints they bring back from the real system. Make the case for what should be built once for everyone, hand it to our Product Engineers with a proper specification, and confirm it solves the problem it came from. Support the Senior Project Manager and Project Manager on technical feasibility, effort and sequencing. Stay on the account through the first go-live, and hand over a solution design that is documented and maintainable. Feed recurring customer requirements back to Product so the standard grows in the right direction. What We're Really Looking For The following key attributes ensure success in this role: Relentless on Clarity – You do not accept a vague answer as an answer, and you keep going until the requirement is specific enough to build on. Architectural Judgment – You can tell the difference between a requirement that deserves a custom solution and one that deserves a conversation. Credibility with Architects – You hold your own with a customer's enterprise architect and earn their trust rather than deferring to them. Clear Recommendations – You frame a difficult scope question so that the people who decide can actually decide, and you say plainly what you would do. Translation – You move between a business requirement and a technical design in both directions without losing anything. Long-Term Thinking – You design for what the customer will need in two years, not only for what unblocks the current wave. What You Bring Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field. 4+ years of experience in solution design, technical consulting, enterprise integration or a technical product role. Solid understanding of enterprise system landscapes: ERP systems, interfaces, master data, and how data actually moves between them. Hands-on experience configuring integrations on an integration platform, or comparable low-code or configuration-driven work. Experience writing specifications that engineers can build from without a translation layer. Track record of driving technical clarity in a project setting, including escalating early and constructively. Comfortable in customer-facing technical discussions with senior IT stakeholders. Fluent in German and English, spoken and written. Bonus points for hands-on experience with SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or comparable ERP systems, or with e-invoicing and EDI standards. Benefits High ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path. Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises. Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily. Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression. Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option program. Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators. Technology exposure – be at the forefront of AI and enjoy continuous learning opportunities. Visits & offsites – paid visits and stays at our HQ in Zurich, including collaborative team offsites. Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact. Learn more about blp and our values at https://blp.digital/company/careers . Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Werkstudent KI & Automatisierung (m/w/d)
description: Stellenbeschreibung Hi, ich bin Felix Lippe. Vor ein paar Jahren habe ich Lippe Personal gegründet. Heute sind wir über 25 Leute und eine der führenden Recruiting-Agenturen für medizinische Praxen in Deutschland: Ärzte, Zahnärzte, Physiotherapeuten, Pflege. Wir haben in den letzten Jahren hunderte Praxen betreut und tausende Bewerbungen für unsere Kunden generiert. Das Geschäft läuft. Und jetzt kommt der Teil, warum ich diese Stelle ausschreibe. Ich baue das Unternehmen gerade grundlegend um: weg von manueller Arbeit, hin zu einem KI-gesteuerten Unternehmen. Nicht als Buzzword auf der Website, sondern als echtes Projekt, an dem ich täglich selbst arbeite – mit Tools wie Claude Code, n8n und einem eigenen KI-Setup. Ich tausche mich dazu laufend mit externen KI-Agenturen und Experten aus, ich stecke tief im Thema. Was mir fehlt, ist nicht das Wissen und sind nicht die Ideen. Was mir fehlt, ist Zeit und eine rechte Hand, die mit mir baut. Genau das ist diese Stelle. Die Rolle: Werkstudent mit Founder-Associate-Charakter Du arbeitest nicht „bei uns in der IT". Du arbeitest mit mir. Direkt, auf Geschäftsführer-Ebene, ohne Hierarchie-Ebenen dazwischen. Konkret heißt das: Wir schauen uns gemeinsam an, wo im Unternehmen noch manuell gearbeitet wird, und dann bauen wir das weg. Du bekommst von mir klare Briefings, setzt eigenständig um, und wir sprechen uns in einem festen wöchentlichen Termin ab – oft auch öfter, weil ich Sparring liebe. Du bist bei strategischen Themen dabei, verstehst, warum wir Dinge tun, und siehst, wie ein Unternehmen von innen umgebaut wird. raw.title: Werkstudent KI & Automatisierung (m/w/d)
raw.description:
Stellenbeschreibung

Hi, ich bin Felix Lippe.

Vor ein paar Jahren habe ich Lippe Personal gegründet. Heute sind wir über 25 Leute und eine der führenden Recruiting-Agenturen für medizinische Praxen in Deutschland: Ärzte, Zahnärzte, Physiotherapeuten, Pflege. Wir haben in den letzten Jahren hunderte Praxen betreut und tausende Bewerbungen für unsere Kunden generiert. Das Geschäft läuft.

Und jetzt kommt der Teil, warum ich diese Stelle ausschreibe.

Ich baue das Unternehmen gerade grundlegend um: weg von manueller Arbeit, hin zu einem KI-gesteuerten Unternehmen. Nicht als Buzzword auf der Website, sondern als echtes Projekt, an dem ich täglich selbst arbeite – mit Tools wie Claude Code, n8n und einem eigenen KI-Setup. Ich tausche mich dazu laufend mit externen KI-Agenturen und Experten aus, ich stecke tief im Thema. Was mir fehlt, ist nicht das Wissen und sind nicht die Ideen. Was mir fehlt, ist Zeit und eine rechte Hand, die mit mir baut.

Genau das ist diese Stelle.

Die Rolle: Werkstudent mit Founder-Associate-Charakter

Du arbeitest nicht „bei uns in der IT". Du arbeitest mit mir. Direkt, auf Geschäftsführer-Ebene, ohne Hierarchie-Ebenen dazwischen.

Konkret heißt das: Wir schauen uns gemeinsam an, wo im Unternehmen noch manuell gearbeitet wird, und dann bauen wir das weg. Du bekommst von mir klare Briefings, setzt eigenständig um, und wir sprechen uns in einem festen wöchentlichen Termin ab – oft auch öfter, weil ich Sparring liebe. Du bist bei strategischen Themen dabei, verstehst, warum wir Dinge tun, und siehst, wie ein Unternehmen von innen umgebaut wird. Wenn ich mich mit externen KI-Agenturen und Experten austausche, bekommst du das mit und lernst direkt daraus – genau wie ich.

Das ist der Deal: Du hebelst meine Zeit, ich gebe dir Einblicke und Verantwortung, die du als Werkstudent sonst nirgendwo bekommst.


Deine Aufgaben

  • Du baust mit KI-Tools (vor allem Claude Code) Automatisierungen für unser Tagesgeschäft: Bewerbermanagement, Reporting, Anzeigenerstellung

  • Du optimierst, automatisierst und digitalisierst Prozesse quer durchs Unternehmen – vom Vertrieb bis zum Fulfillment

  • Du setzt Workflows in n8n auf und verbindest unsere Tools miteinander (Airtable, HubSpot, GitHub)

  • Du dokumentierst, was du baust, so dass es als System im Unternehmen bleibt und wächst

  • Du bist mein Sparringspartner: Wir entwickeln gemeinsam weiter, wie dieses Unternehmen in zwei Jahren arbeitet

Was ich dir biete

  • 20 Euro pro Stunde – bewusst am oberen Ende für Werkstudenten in Düsseldorf, weil ich lieber einen richtig Guten habe als drei Mittelmäßige

  • 16 bis 20 Stunden pro Woche, flexibel um deinen Vorlesungsplan herum, in den Semesterferien gerne mehr

  • Nach der Einarbeitung weitgehend Homeoffice. Unser Office in Düsseldorf steht dir jederzeit offen

  • Professionelles KI-Setup ab Tag eins (u. a. Claude Code Max Plan) – du arbeitest mit Tools, die die meisten Unternehmen noch nicht mal kennen

  • Direkter Zugang zu allem, was ich lerne: aus dem Austausch mit KI-Agenturen, Experten und aus unseren eigenen Projekten

  • Echte Verantwortung statt Praktikanten-Aufgaben: Was du baust, läuft danach jeden Tag in einem echten Unternehmen

  • Eine Erfahrung, die dich von praktisch jedem Absolventen abhebt: Du hast nicht über digitale Transformation gelesen, du hast eine mitgebaut

So läuft der Bewerbungsprozess

Bitte kein klassisches Anschreiben, das liest hier keiner. Stattdessen:

  1. Bewerbung über das Formular – Lebenslauf plus (das ist mir am wichtigsten) ein Link zu irgendetwas, das du gebaut hast: GitHub-Repo, kleines Tool, Automatisierung, Uni-Projekt. Größe egal. Dazu zwei, drei Sätze, was du zuletzt mit KI gelöst hast

  2. Probeaufgabe – wenn deine Bewerbung passt, bekommst du eine kleine Aufgabe (zwei bis drei Stunden Aufwand)

  3. 30-Minuten-Call mit mir – wir lernen uns kennen, du stellst deine Fragen

  4. Entscheidung innerhalb von 48 Stunden. Versprochen

Ich freue mich auf dich.

Felix Lippe
Geschäftsführer, Lippe Personal GmbH


Dein Profil

Ich halte das bewusst offen, weil mir deine Denkweise wichtiger ist als dein Lebenslauf:

  • Du bist eingeschriebener Vollzeit-Student, zum Beispiel in Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Data Science oder etwas Vergleichbarem. Auch andere Studiengänge sind okay, wenn du technisch unterwegs bist

  • Du hast schon mal mit KI-Tools wie Claude Code, Cursor oder ChatGPT etwas Eigenes gebaut oder automatisiert. Muss nichts Großes sein, aber du solltest es zeigen können

  • Begriffe wie Git und Terminal schrecken dich nicht ab

  • Du denkst unternehmerisch: Du fragst nicht „was soll ich tun?", sondern „was bringt uns weiter?"

  • Du arbeitest selbstständig und brauchst niemanden, der dir dreimal am Tag über die Schulter schaut

  • Sehr gutes Deutsch in Wort und Schrift

Falls du denkst „ich habe noch nie professionell programmiert": völlig okay. Ich suche keinen fertigen Entwickler. Ich suche jemanden, der mit KI-Tools umgehen kann, Prozesse versteht und Lust hat, mit einem Gründer ein Unternehmen umzubauen. Das ist ein eigenes Handwerk – und ehrlich gesagt eines der wertvollsten, die man 2026 lernen kann.

You report to our CTO and are the voice of the platform in engineering decisions. How we build and run things Everything runs on Kubernetes (Azure AKS), deployed with Helm and GitOps/Flux. All infrastructure is Terraform, applied through CI. CI/CD for every service on GitLab Managed services wherever they keep life simple: Postgres, OpenSearch, Redis, blob storage. We self-host only where it clearly pays off. Two clouds: Azure as our primary cloud, AWS for search and mail ingestion. Python everywhere: read and fix application code when that is where the fix belongs. Security is routine: automated scanning in every pipeline, regular external pentests, quarterly backup and disaster-recovery tests. You decide how this platform evolves, you keep it secure, observable and cost-efficient, and you extend it as the product grows. Most recently that meant an LLM gateway with region failover in front of our Azure OpenAI deployments, and performing GPU capacity planning for our own models.

You set your own roadmap. Infrastructure at Workist is run as quarterly themes that you propose, make the case for and deliver, and roughly a third of your time goes to whatever the week brings: an incident, a pentest finding, a developer whose deployment is stuck and needs a second pair of eyes. You report to our CTO and are the voice of the platform in engineering decisions.


How we build and run things

  • Everything runs on Kubernetes (Azure AKS), deployed with Helm and GitOps/Flux. All infrastructure is Terraform, applied through CI.

  • CI/CD for every service on GitLab

  • Managed services wherever they keep life simple: Postgres, OpenSearch, Redis, blob storage. We self-host only where it clearly pays off.

  • Two clouds: Azure as our primary cloud, AWS for search and mail ingestion.

  • Python everywhere: read and fix application code when that is where the fix belongs.

  • Security is routine: automated scanning in every pipeline, regular external pentests, quarterly backup and disaster-recovery tests.


Your responsibilities

Own the platform

  • Own the architecture of our cloud environments across Azure and AWS: how subscriptions, networks, identities and environments are structured and stay isolated

  • Design and deliver the platform capabilities the product needs next, from GPU capacity and an LLM gateway to new environments

  • Set the standard for how we run Kubernetes and our managed data services: capacity planned ahead of growth, changes and upgrades rolled out safely and routinely, costs kept in check

Keep it quiet

  • Own the security posture end to end: least-privilege access, network isolation, findings from scanners and pentests, and a patch cadence that runs itself. Be a technical counterpart for audits and security questionnaires

  • Own observability and alerting so that every alert is worth acting on, and lead the response to platform incidents including the follow-up fixes

  • Run quarterly backup/restore and disaster-recovery tests, and close what they reveal

Make the team faster

  • Own the path from merge request to production: fast builds, reliable deployments, environments and access on demand

  • Build the infrastructure behind our AI models: the LLM gateway, model deployments with region failover, GPU capacity, and whatever the next model needs


What this looked like recently: a Redis instance that silently dropped half of its new TCP connections and took the Celery workers down with it, region failover and load balancing for our Azure OpenAI deployments, moving our clusters from nginx ingress to the Kubernetes Gateway API.


Your profile

We're looking for a professional team player who thrives in an environment where we share knowledge openly and push each other to deliver the best possible outcome. What you bring:


  • You have run production infrastructure for years, ideally as the person who owned it end to end rather than one of many in a large ops team

  • Kubernetes and Terraform in production: cluster upgrades, Helm, GitOps, and infrastructure as code for a whole cloud estate

  • Production experience on Azure or AWS. Most of our estate is Azure, so an AWS background works if you are willing to go deep on Azure.

  • Active Python skills: you read and debug a Python codebase and fix the application when the application is what is broken

  • Security as a habit: you have run patch management, handled pentest findings and designed least-privilege access, and you prioritise findings pragmatically

  • You write clearly: runbooks, incident write-ups and architecture decisions that others can follow

raw.description:
Das erwartet Dich bei uns

Stitch, POV und Voiceover sind für Dich keine Fremdwörter und Du weißt, wie man Geschichten im Hochkant-Format erzählt, die nicht nur gut aussehen, sondern auch performen? Du fühlst Dich in der Beauty-Branche zu Hause, hast ein Gespür für Trends und Zielgruppen und möchtest Social Media für starke Marken aktiv mitgestalten und weiterentwickeln?
 
Dann freuen wir uns auf Deine Bewerbung – und ganz besonders auf ein kurzes Vorstellungsvideo (max. 60 Sekunden), in dem Du Dich kreativ präsentierst und uns Deine Persönlichkeit zeigst.
 
Am besten schickst Du uns mit Deinen Unterlagen einen Link zu Deinem Video – zum Beispiel über Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, YouTube (nicht gelistet) oder Loom. Bitte stelle sicher, dass wir das Video über den Link auch ansehen können.
 
Als Senior Social Media Manager (m/w/d) übernimmst Du Verantwortung für die strategische und operative Weiterentwicklung unserer Social-Media-Kanäle und Marken. Die Position ist auf zwei Jahre befristet. Du verbindest kreatives Gespür mit einem datengetriebenen Blick auf Performance und entwickelst Content, der unsere Zielgruppen begeistert und unsere Marken auf Instagram & TikTok sichtbar macht.

  • Du übernimmst die eigenständige Betreuung und Weiterentwicklung unserer Social-Media-Kanäle und Marken – von der strategischen Ausrichtung und Redaktionsplanung über die Content-Produktion bis hin zu Community Management und Reporting
  • Du entwickelst kreative Social-Media-Konzepte und Content-Strategien, die auf die jeweiligen Marken, Zielgruppen und Business-Ziele einzahlen
  • Du entwickelst eigenständig Content-Ideen und Formate und setzt diese von der ersten Idee bis zum fertigen Posting um
  • Du stehst nicht nur hinter der Kamera, sondern auch selbstbewusst vor der Kamera und produzierst authentischen, plattformgerechten Content für unsere Social-Media-Kanäle
  • Du fotografierst, filmst und editierst eigenständig Bilder und Videos rund um unsere Produkte für Instagram & TikTok
  • Du hast aktuelle Social-Media-Trends, Formate, Creator und Plattform-Entwicklungen im Blick und bewertest, welche davon für unsere Marken relevant sind
  • Du analysierst relevante Social-Media-KPIs und Performance-Daten, leitest daraus konkrete Learnings ab und optimierst unsere Inhalte kontinuierlich
  • Du hast unsere Wettbewerber und den Markt im Blick und bringst daraus neue Impulse für unsere Marken und deren Social-Auftritte ein
  • Du entwickelst unsere Marken auf Social Media kontinuierlich weiter und stellst sicher, dass Tonalität, Look & Feel und Content-Strategie konsistent sind
  • Du arbeitest eng mit internen Teams und externen Partnern zusammen und bringst Social-Media-Perspektiven aktiv in übergreifende Projekte ein
  • Du übernimmst Verantwortung für eigene Projekte und treibst diese eigenständig voran – von der Konzeption bis zur Umsetzung und Erfolgsmessung
  • Du führst und entwickelst Mitarbeitende, gibst Feedback, unterstützt bei ihrer Weiterentwicklung und schaffst gemeinsam mit dem Team die Grundlage für starke Ergebnisse


Das bringst Du mit

  • Du hast mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Social-Media-Management, idealerweise auf Unternehmens- oder Agenturseite, und hast bereits eigenständig Social-Media-Kanäle und Marken betreut
  • Du kennst Dich mit Instagram und TikTok bestens aus und weißt, was guten Social Content ausmacht – von relevanten Trends bis hin zu plattformspezifischen Formaten
  • Du hast ein starkes Gespür für kreative Konzepte, Storytelling, Trends, Ästhetik und zielgruppengerechten Content
  • Du hast Erfahrung darin, Social-Media-Strategien und Content-Konzepte eigenständig zu entwickeln und umzusetzen
  • Du produzierst gerne selbst Content und hast Erfahrung in der Foto- und Videoproduktion sowie im Editing, z. B. mit CapCut, Canva oder Adobe Creative Cloud
  • Du fühlst Dich vor der Kamera wohl und hast keine Scheu, selbst Content zu produzieren und unsere Produkte authentisch zu präsentieren
  • Du hast ein gutes Verständnis für Social-Media-KPIs und kannst Performance-Daten analysieren, Learnings ableiten und daraus konkrete Handlungsempfehlungen für zukünftigen Content entwickeln
  • Du hast bereits erste Führungserfahrung gesammelt und Freude daran, Kolleg:innen zu unterstützen, Verantwortung zu übertragen und gemeinsam Ergebnisse zu erzielen
  • Du arbeitest eigenständig, strukturiert und lösungsorientiert und übernimmst Verantwortung für Deine Projekte
  • Du bist kommunikationsstark, engagiert und kreativ und hast Spaß daran, eigene Ideen einzubringen und diese auch umzusetzen
  • Du arbeitest gerne cross-funktional und kannst unterschiedliche Stakeholder für Deine Ideen begeistern
  • Du besitzt hervorragende Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sowie sehr gute Englischkenntnisse
  • Du wohnst in München oder Umgebung, 100% remote ist nicht möglich


Das bieten wir Dir

  • Verantwortung ab Tag eins: Arbeite mit einem kreativen, hochmotivierten Team an Themen am Puls der Zeit – hier gestaltest Du aktiv mit!
  • Internationales Flair & Start-up Vibes: Agiles Arbeiten in einem globalen Umfeld mit echter „Du“-Kultur und flachen Hierarchien
  • Dein Wachstum, Dein Weg: Bringe eigene Ideen ein und nutze Dein persönliches Entwicklungsbudget, um genau das zu lernen, was Dich weiterbringt
  • Kein Tag wie der andere: Vielfältige, spannende Projekte in einem dynamischen, wachstumsstarken Unternehmen
  • Innovationen zum Anfassen: Entdecke angesagte Trendprodukte zum Vorteilspreis – plus jede Menge Freebies
  • Dein Wohlfühl Boost: Profitiere von starken Fitness-Deals, Fahrradleasing, Corporate Benefits und Rabatt bei unseren Partnerfriseuren
  • Late Night im Office? Kein Problem: Dein Abendessen geht auf uns. Einfach bestellen und weitermachen, wenn’s mal länger dauert
  • Deutschlandticket? Sharing is caring: Wir bezuschussen Dein Ticket für maximale Mobilität
  • Work your way: Modern ausgestattetes Office im Herzen von München und Homeoffice inklusive


Dein Weg zu uns

Dein Weg zu uns

  • Languages & Architecture: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, MVVM, Clean Architecture
  • Networking & Data: GraphQL, Firebase Remote Config, Crashlytics
  • Dependency Injection: Dagger/Hilt
  • Testing: Espresso, Robolectric, JUnit
  • CI/CD & Automation: GitLab CI/CD, Fastlane, Docker
  • Collaboration Tools: Figma, Microsoft Teams, Atlassin Jira, Confluence, Atlas etc

About the Role

  • Design, Develop, and Maintain high-quality Android applications with a focus on scalability, performance, and user experience
  • Collaborate closely and effectively with iOS, Backend, and Feature based Teams to align on feature specifications and ensure smooth cross-platform integration
  • Drive technical improvements across the entire codebase, including architecture enhancements and codebase modernization and prepare/maintain technical documentation as and when required
  • Enhance app performance and user experience through UI optimizations, accessibility compliance, and improvements in battery usage, memory management, and load times with focus on an excellent customer experience and delivering high quality products
  • Leverage analytics & metrics to make data-driven decisions, optimizing performance and engagement based on user behavior and app health
  • Mentor and support fellow engineers, promoting a culture of technical excellence, and collaboration through code reviews and sharing best practices
  • Stay up to date with the latest Android trends, tools, and technologies, incorporating innovative solutions to improve the team's workflow and drive mobile development excellence

About You

  • 6+ years of extensive experience and strong expertise in Kotlin (Jetpack Compose, MVVM, Coroutines), with a deep understanding of Android architecture, best practices along with SOLID principles and software architecture patterns etc
  • Experience with testing (unit, integration, UI testing) and a strong commitment to writing testable, maintainable, high-quality code.
  • Ability to drive technical strategy ensuring high standards in code quality, performance, and scalability, focusing on product impact with proper documentation (RFCs, POCs, SOPs etc) and improve processes as needed e.g, incident management, release processes etc
  • Customer-centric approach with a focus on delivering great user experiences and strong collaboration skills to work closely with iOS, Backend, and Hybrid teams.
  • Continuous Learner's Mindset: Willingness to learn new tools, technologies, and frameworks as mobile development evolves.

Nice to have

  • Experience with hybrid frameworks/platforms (Kotlin Multiplatform Mobile, React Native) and understanding their architecture.
  • Experience with GraphQL, REST APIs, and integrating backend services.
  • Experience in UI/UX design or a good eye for design principles and user interface consistency.

title: Langfuse - Product Engineer, Integrations
description: Why Integrations Engineering at Langfuse Your work puts Langfuse into developers’ hands. Our SDKs are downloaded 26M+ times per month, and for many developers the first thing they touch is an integration — a few lines of code that connect their favorite framework to Langfuse. When that experience is seamless, they’re wow’ed. When it’s not, we might have lost them. You’ll own that critical first impression across 40+ framework integrations. You’ll live at the frontier of LLM application development. The AI framework ecosystem moves fast — new agent frameworks, orchestration libraries, and model providers emerge every week. You’ll be among the first to instrument them, giving you unmatched exposure to how cutting-edge AI applications are built. The developers you serve are some of the most ambitious software engineers in the world, and working closely with them will make you an expert on LLM engineering yourself. Everything you build is open source and immediately visible. All Langfuse integrations are MIT-licensed. When you ship a new integration or improve an existing one, thousands of developers benefit the same day — and they’ll tell you about it in GitHub issues, on Twitter, and in our community channels. What You’ll Do Build and maintain framework integrations. Langfuse integrates with 40+ frameworks and model providers: OpenAI SDK, Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Pydantic AI, OpenAI Agents, CrewAI, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, LiveKit, and many more. You’ll own these integrations end-to-end — from initial implementation to ongoing maintenance as frameworks evolve. When a new framework gains traction, you’ll be among the first to instrument it. Design new integration patterns for emerging frameworks. When a framework or a new agent orchestrator appears, you’ll evaluate it, design the right instrumentation approach (callback handler, decorator, OTEL auto-instrumentation, or a combination), build the integration, write the docs, and ship it. You’ll develop strong opinions on what makes a great integration experience. Contribute to the core SDKs. While integrations are your primary focus, your work will surface needs in our Python and TypeScript SDKs. You’ll contribute improvements to the core SDK when your integration work demands it — whether that’s a new hook point, better context propagation, or performance optimizations. Write documentation and integration guides. At Langfuse, docs are part of our core product. When you ship a new integration, the guide ships with it. You’ll own the integration docs, quickstart tutorials, cookbooks, and migration paths that help developers get started in minutes. Be a voice in the developer community. You’ll engage with framework communities, respond to integration-related GitHub issues, write blog posts about new integrations, and be present in our Slack/Discord channels. You’ll build relationships with framework maintainers and represent Langfuse in the broader AI developer ecosystem. What We’re Looking For Passionate about the LLM ecosystem. You’ve built real applications with frameworks like LangChain, Pydantic AI, Vercel AI SDK, LlamaIndex, or similar — or you have a deep willingness to go deep and get your hands dirty with every major framework in the space. You’re excited about this ecosystem, not just familiar with it. Strong in Python and/or TypeScript. You write clean, reliable code. You don’t need to be a systems-level performance expert, but you care about code quality and understand that integrations run inside other people’s production systems. Product-minded engineer. You think about the developer who’s going to use your integration at 11pm trying to ship a feature. You obsess over the getting-started experience: how many lines of code does it take? Is the error message helpful? Does the docs example actually work? Self-directed and motivated. You know how to develop conviction about what to build and how to ship it. You don’t wait for detailed specs — you investigate the framework, talk to users, and propose the right approach. Excited about open source and developer community. You genuinely enjoy talking to developers about their integration challenges, writing clear documentation, and contributing to open source projects. Thrives in a small, accountable team. Your output is visible and matters. You’re comfortable owning outcomes, not just tasks. CS or quantitative degree preferred, but not required. We care far more about what you’ve built and your hunger to learn. Bonus Points Experience with OpenTelemetry internals or observability instrumentation Contributions to popular open source projects, SDKs, or developer tools Experience building developer tooling, CLIs, or client libraries Former founder or early startup experience Active presence in AI/ML developer communities (blog posts, talks, open source) No candidate checks all boxes. If you feel you are a good fit for this role, please go ahead and apply. Projects You Could Own Build and ship a Langfuse integration for an emerging agent framework (e.g., OpenClaw, new OTEL-based instrumentation) Design the integration pattern for a new category of AI tools (e.g., voice agents via LiveKit/Pipecat) Create comprehensive quickstart cookbooks that get developers from zero to traced in under 5 minutes Work with the OpenTelemetry community to improve GenAI semantic conventions Maintain and upgrade our most popular integrations (OpenAI, LangChain, Vercel AI SDK) as those frameworks ship breaking changes Perks Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries. Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare. Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options. Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries. A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee. Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites. Culture - We All Shape It As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture. Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here . Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.   • Product-minded engineer. You think about the developer who’s going to use your integration at 11pm trying to ship a feature. You obsess over the getting-started experience: how many lines of code does it take? Is the error message helpful? Does the docs example actually work?

  • Self-directed and motivated. You know how to develop conviction about what to build and how to ship it. You don’t wait for detailed specs — you investigate the framework, talk to users, and propose the right approach.

  • Excited about open source and developer community. You genuinely enjoy talking to developers about their integration challenges, writing clear documentation, and contributing to open source projects.

  • Thrives in a small, accountable team. Your output is visible and matters. You’re comfortable owning outcomes, not just tasks.

CS or quantitative degree preferred, but not required. We care far more about what you’ve built and your hunger to learn.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with OpenTelemetry internals or observability instrumentation

  • Contributions to popular open source projects, SDKs, or developer tools

  • Experience building developer tooling, CLIs, or client libraries

  • Former founder or early startup experience

  • Active presence in AI/ML developer communities (blog posts, talks, open source)

 

No candidate checks all boxes. If you feel you are a good fit for this role, please go ahead and apply.

 

Projects You Could Own

opportunities.</li> <li>Excellent outbound prospecting and territory-building discipline.</li> <li>Willingness to travel extensively across Europe.</li> </ul> <p>Experience selling into logistics, description: Company Description We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. The role Checkout.com is looking for an enthusiastic Engineer I to join Finance Technology with a focus on Workday Adaptive Planning . Adaptive Planning supports finance, workforce, sales, and operational planning, giving teams a shared platform for budgeting, forecasting, modelling, reporting, and decision-making. This is an early-career engineering role for someone who wants to build depth in finance systems, application configuration, data integration, and operational support. You will work with Finance, Finance Technology, Data, and wider Corporate Technology teams to keep planning processes reliable, well-controlled, and easy to operate. You will have support from more senior engineers for complex design decisions, but you will be expected to work independently for longer periods on well-defined configuration, integration, support, and continuous-improvement tasks. This reflects Checkout’s Engineer 1 expectations: delivering small-to-medium-sized work, supporting common operational flows, communicating clearly, and taking ownership of the quality of what you deliver. How you’ll make an impact Configure, maintain, and enhance Adaptive Planning models, dimensions, versions, levels, accounts, sheets, reports, dashboards, and planning workflows under appropriate guidance. Support the delivery of budgeting, forecasting, headcount planning, scenario modelling, and management reporting capabilities for Finance and business stakeholders. Build and support data loads and integrations between Adaptive Planning, Workday Financials, Workday HCM, and other approved internal or third-party systems. Maintain data mappings, transformation rules, validation checks, and reconciliation processes so that planning data is complete, accurate, and traceable. Monitor scheduled loads and integration tasks, investigate failures, and resolve common data or configuration issues within agreed service levels. Triage incidents and service requests, identifying root causes and escalating complex or high-risk issues with clear evidence and recommended next steps. Partner with Finance stakeholders to understand requirements and translate them into maintainable system configuration, reporting, or integration changes. Contribute to the assessment and delivery of future analytics data flows, including the potential use of Adaptive Planning data in BigQuery and management analytics. Participate in testing, regression testing, release preparation, and controlled deployment of Adaptive Planning changes. Follow change-control, access-management, data-quality, and audit requirements relevant to financial systems and planning data. Create clear documentation, support guides, data dictionaries, integration runbooks, and knowledge-base articles so that operational knowledge is shared rather than held by one person. Identify recurring manual work or failure patterns and propose practical automation and process improvements. What we’re looking for Essential experience and skills Experience in a finance systems, enterprise applications, data, reporting, or integration environment. Practical experience with Workday Adaptive Planning, or strong experience with a comparable planning, performance-management, ERP, or finance application and a clear ability to learn Adaptive quickly. Understanding of core finance planning concepts such as budgets, forecasts, actuals, variance analysis, allocations, dimensions, hierarchies, and scenarios. Experience configuring or supporting structured data models, application workflows, reports, dashboards, or business rules. Ability to work with data imports, exports, mappings, transformations, validations, and reconciliations. Strong troubleshooting skills, with the ability to break down an issue, gather evidence, identify likely causes, and communicate findings clearly. Good attention to detail and an understanding of why accuracy, access control, auditability, and repeatability matter in finance systems. Ability to manage small-to-medium-sized tasks independently while knowing when to ask for help or escalate. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with Finance and Technology stakeholders. Desirable experience Workday Adaptive Planning certification or implementation experience. Experience with Adaptive Planning Integration, Planning Data Loader, APIs, or equivalent enterprise planning integration tooling. Experience integrating planning systems with Workday Financials, Workday HCM, an ERP, a data warehouse, or a reporting platform. Familiarity with SOX controls, financial audit requirements, data privacy, and segregation of duties. Experience supporting month-end, budget, forecast, or management-reporting cycles. Exposure to Agile delivery, ticket-driven change management, incident management, or service-management practices. Diagnose and resolve routine integration or data-quality issues using a structured troubleshooting approach. Deliver small-to-medium-sized enhancements from requirement clarification through testing, documentation, and controlled release. Explain key planning data flows, mappings, dependencies, and operational controls to Finance and Technology colleagues. Improve the reliability or efficiency of at least one recurring planning or finance-technology process. Maintain accurate, useful documentation and contribute positively to team ceremonies, reviews, and knowledge-sharing sessions. Looks for durable automation and simpler operating processes rather than repeatedly working around the same manual problem. Why join Finance Technology? You will work on systems that sit at the centre of how Checkout.com plans, forecasts, reports, and makes financial decisions. The role offers the opportunity to develop a broad foundation across enterprise applications, finance processes, integrations, data quality, controls, and automation while working closely with experienced Finance and Technology professionals. Life at Checkout.com We understand that work is just one part of your life.
